input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view in the Dashboard (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

This epic delivers the run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users can select two or more training and pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side, and switch to a diff view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. Today parameters and metrics live only on per-run pages, forcing comparison via exported spreadsheets; this epic makes comparison a first-class platform workflow that model promotion decisions can rely on.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- Side-by-side view of parameters and metrics for the selected runs.
- Diff mode for two selected runs that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them (the diff view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface, delivered together with the side-by-side view).
- The comparison works for both training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs. Data Science Pipelines is a passive component here — its run metadata is consumed as-is through existing interfaces, with no code change to Data Science Pipelines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more runs selected from the Dashboard runs list, when the user opens the comparison, then the parameters and metrics of all selected runs are displayed side by side.
- Given two runs selected for comparison, when the user switches to the diff view, then the parameters and metrics that differ between the two runs are highlighted.
- Given a selection that includes pipeline runs and training runs, then parameters and metrics render for both run types in the comparison.
- The comparison for pipeline runs requires no code change to Data Science Pipelines components (passive-component validation).
- No regression to existing per-run parameter and metric pages.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the run diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data as HLR-1 — it is not separately schedulable and ships in this epic.

# Run lineage link-back on registered model versions

## Description

This epic makes registered model versions link back to the run that produced them. The Model Registry becomes the source of truth for training lineage: every model version registered from a training or pipeline run carries a reference to that run, exposed through the Model Registry REST API so any consumer — including the Dashboard's registry UI — can resolve which run produced a given version and open a comparison from it.

## Scope

- Capture the reference to the producing run (training run or pipeline run) on registered model versions at registration time, using the documented extension point for structured metadata on model versions (custom properties).
- Expose the run reference through the Model Registry REST API so it is retrievable on model version views by platform consumers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, then the version carries a reference to the producing run that is retrievable via the Model Registry REST API.
- Given a model version registered from a pipeline run, the lineage reference works the same as for training runs.
- Given existing model versions that have no run reference, then they remain valid and retrievable (backward compatible; no migration required to keep the registry functional).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. This epic delivers the registry-side lineage; the registry-UI entry point that opens the comparison is delivered by the Dashboard-side epic for HLR-2.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry entry point into the run comparison capability. In the Dashboard-rendered registry UI, a registered model version shows the run that produced it (training or pipeline run), with an action that opens the run comparison view for that run — so a comparison can be started directly from the Model Registry while evaluating candidate model versions for promotion, not only from the runs list.

## Scope

- Surface the run lineage reference stored on registered model versions in the registry UI (which the Dashboard renders).
- Entry point on the model version view that opens the run comparison view with the producing run loaded, letting the user complete the comparison selection there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a run lineage reference, then the registry UI displays the producing run.
- Given the lineage entry point on a model version, when the user activates it, then the run comparison view opens with the producing run loaded.
- Given a model version without a run reference, then the version view renders without the lineage entry point (graceful degradation, no error state).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. This epic delivers the registry-UI entry point; the lineage storage and API exposure on model versions is delivered by the Model Registry-side epic for HLR-2.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic documents the run comparison workflow end to end, from both entry points: starting a comparison from the runs list in the Dashboard, and opening a comparison from the Model Registry via a model version's run lineage. It gives data scientists the guidance they currently lack when they fall back to exported spreadsheets, covering both training runs and pipeline runs.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparison from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and using the diff view to see what changed between two runs.
- Comparison from the Model Registry: reading a model version's run lineage and opening the comparison for the producing run.
- Coverage of both run types — training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs — wherever the workflow differs between them.
- Cross-references from existing run pages and model registry documentation into the comparison workflow topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow from the runs list and from the Model Registry, including the side-by-side and diff views.
- The documentation covers the workflow for both training runs and pipeline runs.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of the comparison view, the model version run lineage, and the registry entry point before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry.
